one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall in the window, both on 2026-10-28: Q3 2026 earnings and the FOMC decision. 2026-10-31 is a Saturday, so the close that counts is 2026-10-30. Earnings: consensus is about $4.07-4.15 EPS on about $10.8B revenue. That revenue figure looks low: 1H26 revenue was $20.4B ($9.3B + $11.1B) against a $45.5-46.5B full-year guide, which implies about $25.6B in 2H. So revenue has room to beat, but Q4 usually carries the year. At Laguna (2026-09-16) the CEO flagged strong Q3 orders and said the $200B backlog comes 'very early in 2027'. Investors already expect this, so the surprise will come from margins and EPS, where GEV has missed in 3 of the last 8 quarters. GEV's earnings reactions run large in both directions (+14% after Q1 2026, -9% after Q2 2026). FOMC: the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, and the dot plot signals one more hike in 2026. Prediction markets price October at hold 74% / hike 26% (Kalshi/Polymarket via defirate, 2026-10-01), with December the likelier hike. Price action: the stock is up 12.9% from the $874.76 close on 9/14 (the GLJ Sell day), including +3.9% on 10/1 after Evercore raised estimates. Short-term reversal and momentum roughly cancel. I centre the distribution near $990, essentially flat, with a 15% one-month log sigma (slightly above annual vol / 3.5 = 14.9%, to allow for the earnings gap), symmetric in log space. This is unchanged from round 1 apart from the corrected low-close fact.

fair_value.method: Blend of NTM P/E (Oct-2027 NTM EPS about $31.0 x 33x = $1,023), EV/EBITDA (2028E EBITDA $11.8B x 22x + $11B end-2027 net cash, over about 262M shares = $1,033) and FCF yield (2028E FCF about $9.0B at a 3.5% yield = $981), weighted 40/35/25. That gives about $1,015 per share 12 months out, down from $1,120 in round 1 after re-anchoring EBITDA, net cash and FCF to management's 2028 outlook and the reported balance sheet.

inputs_detail.derivation: Midpoint of consensus ($34.33, MarketScreener) and an EPS anchored on management's outlook (about $30.5: $56B revenue x 20% = $11.2B EBITDA, less about $1.5B D&A, plus about $0.3B net interest, 21% tax, about 262M shares). I lean above guidance because management raised the 2026 outlook three times in 2026 (FCF guide went $5.0-5.5B to $6.5-7.5B to $11.5-12.5B). Evercore also raised its 2027-28 estimates 3-4% on 10/1. I do not take full consensus because consensus 2028 revenue (about $61B) is already about 9% above the $56B outlook.
0.25 x $24.78 + 0.75 x $32.5 = $30.6, plus about 1% for Evercore's raise. I dropped the round-1 +2% drift on top of full consensus because the supervisor showed consensus already runs above guidance.

GEV trades at about 40x 2027E today, and peers sit at about 17-24x (Siemens Energy about 16.7x EV/EBITDA). The Fed hiked on 2026-09-16 and signals one more hike (verified), which argues for compression. Record Q2 2026 industry orders and 2032 slots selling argue against a full de-rating to peer levels. Held at 33x; the verified hike does not move it, because I already priced a hiking cycle in round 1.

bear.story: The cycle turns. Orders fade from about 150 GW annualised (Q2 2026) toward Barclays' sustainable 80-90 GW, slot reservations (63 of 116 GW) stop converting, and AI capex digests or the Fed's new hiking cycle (3.75-4.00% after 9/16, one more signalled) bites. The multiple falls to about 20-21x a guidance-level $30-31 2028 EPS, close to Siemens Energy. Precedent: global gas awards fell from about 100 GW in 2000 to about 30 GW by 2003, and GEV fell 15% in a week on DeepSeek (Jan 2025) and 8.6% in a day on GLJ's Sell (9/14/26). GLJ's $470 target is the tail of this case.

base.story: Execution continues. Q3 orders are strong, the $200B backlog arrives very early in 2027, and the January 2027 call shows a larger 2026 change in margin in backlog than 2025's low double digits, plus a 2027 outlook. 2028 EPS settles around $32-33, between guidance and consensus. The multiple compresses to about 33x NTM, so the price rises a little less than earnings.

bull.story: Orders and pricing keep beating: industry orders hold above 120 GW a year, turbine prices keep climbing, and the spring-2027 CMD sets a 2030 outlook that pulls 2028 EPS to about $36. A 38x multiple holds on EPS momentum and the stock clears the $1,196 high, near Evercore's $1,350 and Guggenheim's $1,450 targets after a target-optimism haircut.

thesis_break_reason: At about $650 GEV would trade near 21x a guidance-anchored $31 2028 EPS (management's $56B x 20% outlook), about Siemens Energy's level, so the market would pay no growth premium. That is -34% from here and well beyond 2026's drawdown (June high $1,196 to the $874.76 close on 9/14, -27%). A move that large would most likely mean something fundamental broke: slot reservations failing to convert or orders cancelled, the January 2027 margin-in-backlog disclosure stalling, a hyperscaler capex cut, a large margin miss, or the market concluding the cycle has peaked, as in 2001-02. Kept at $650: re-anchoring EPS to guidance lowers the denominator slightly, but the ~21x no-premium multiple still lands there.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor showed that my round-1 fair value ($1,120) and centre (P(>=987) 0.603, the outlier among five agents) rested on inputs above guidance. MarketScreener's 2028E EBITDA of $13.1B implies about 21.6% margins, against management's $56B x 20% = $11.2B (verified in the 4Q25 8-K). My $17B end-2027 net cash ignored buybacks and the deposit unwind; reported net cash is $10.3B. My $10.5B 2028 FCF sits well above the run rate implied by the >= $24B 2025-28 floor. I verified each point (4Q25 release, 1Q/2Q26 releases, Laguna transcript) and accept them, with one adjustment: management has raised guidance repeatedly, so I anchor between guidance and consensus rather than on guidance alone. Rebuilt methods: P/E $1,023 (NTM EPS $31.0 x 33x), EV/EBITDA $1,033 ($11.8B x 22x + $11B net cash), FCF yield $981 ($9.0B at 3.5%). Blended fair value is $1,015, below the supervisor's ~$1,050 estimate for my corrected blend, because I also cut FCF and net cash on my own reconciliation. I also verified the catalyst calendar: there is no December 2026 update; the 2027 outlook comes on the January call and the CMD with a 2030 outlook in spring 2027 (Laguna). The rerating event stays inside the horizon but comes later, which slightly lowers the 12-month bull weight. Verified the 9/16 Fed hike and the $874.76 low close. Base rates are unchanged: 52% realised vol, a 27% drawdown already in 2026, the 2000-03 order collapse and target-optimism research (Street mean of about $1,237 treated as an upper anchor). Scenarios: 25% bear at $640, 50% base at $1,040, 25% bull at $1,400, as a lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.28/0.20/0.20). That gives a mean of about $1,054, a median of about $1,034 and P(>=987) of 0.557 (was 0.603). I keep it above the other agents' 0.505-0.52 because orders and pricing evidence (record industry orders, margin in backlog rising faster in 2026 than 2025, 2032 slots selling) still tilt the base case slightly up. No options data consulted; nothing under priors/ or round1_capped/ opened.
